findings: Strong ambient, rim and front fill flattened the distinction between lit and shaded faces.
Large emissive interior panels competed with small neon fixtures.
The previous occlusion bake ignored neighbouring assets, so the quay lacked contact shading beneath buildings and the viaduct.
Taxis sat above the road and had no contact shadows.
changes: Reduced broad fill and environment lighting; kept one dominant cool directional key and softer filtered cast shadows.
Reduced room emission separately from neon, increased glass reflectivity and restricted bloom to brighter highlights.
Rebaked nine static assets with district-wide ambient occlusion and a 3.2 m reach; retained the shared atlas and 36 material batches.
Applied restrained baked contact attenuation to diffuse lighting, including unshadowed WebGL area lights.
Aligned taxis with the road and added soft multiplicative contact-shadow planes.

verification.dayNightViews: Visually checked, including close framing and another isometric angle
verification.tests: Passed: existing time, animation, projection, quality-budget and asset checks

performance.environment: RTX 4070, 1225 x 1244 browser viewport, night preset, animation enabled
performance.limitation: Local steady-state measurement; not a physical mobile-device test

renderingLimitations: Area lights do not cast real-time WebGL shadows; baked contact attenuation is an approximation.
Taxi contact shadows are soft planes, not live directional shadow maps.
Interior illumination remains an authored ceiling-falloff texture behind reflective glazing.
